title: DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT OF AN AI-POWERED, POLICY-AWARE EDUCATION AND CAREER PATHWAY INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM FOR SRI LANKAN LEARNERS
aim: The aim of this project is to design, develop, and evaluate an AI-powered, policy-aware Education and Career Pathway Intelligence System that provides personalised, explainable, and accessible education and career guidance for Sri Lankan learners.

objectives.I: To critically review existing literature related to AI-based recommender systems, educational decision-support systems, and career guidance technologies.
objectives.II: To analyse the challenges faced by Sri Lankan learners when navigating educational and career progression pathways.
objectives.III: To design a structured knowledge base representing learner categories, educational pathways, eligibility rules, scholarship information, and career progression routes.
objectives.IV: To develop a hybrid recommendation mechanism combining rule-based eligibility filtering with AI-assisted pathway recommendation and explanation generation.
objectives.V: To implement a web-based prototype capable of generating personalised pathway recommendations, alternative routes, skill-gap insights, and official resource links.
objectives.VI: To integrate accessibility-focused features such as mobile-friendly usability, multilingual support, and voice-assisted interaction.
objectives.VII: To evaluate the proposed system using scenario-based testing, functional testing, and usability feedback.
objectives.VIII: To identify limitations of the proposed solution and recommend future improvements for wider deployment and enhanced AI integration.

main_research_question: How can an AI-powered, policy-aware Education and Career Pathway Intelligence System support Sri Lankan learners through personalised, explainable, and accessible pathway recommendations?

supporting_research_questions.I: How can learner profiles, eligibility requirements and pathway knowledge be integrated to generate suitable recommendations?
supporting_research_questions.II: How can explainable recommendation mechanisms improve user understanding and trust?
supporting_research_questions.III: How can alternative pathway generation and skill-gap identification support educational and career planning?
supporting_research_questions.IV: How can multilingual support, mobile usability and voice-assisted input improve accessibility?
supporting_research_questions.V: How effective is the prototype in providing relevant and usable pathway guidance?

functional_requirements.FR1: Allow users to create learner profiles

scope_paragraphs.168: The proposed system will be developed as a Version 1 web-based prototype designed to support personalised and explainable education and career guidance for Sri Lankan learners. The scope of the project is intentionally controlled to ensure technical feasibility within the timeframe of an undergraduate final-year project while still demonstrating meaningful functionality and innovation.
scope_paragraphs.170: The system will primarily target A/L students, vocational learners, and early-career users seeking educational or career progression guidance. The prototype will initially focus on selected domains including Information Technology, Business and Management, and Engineering.

scope_paragraphs.181: and accessibility-focused interaction features such as mobile-friendly usability and basic voice-assisted input.
scope_paragraphs.183: The recommendation process will utilise structured pathway knowledge, rule-based eligibility filtering, and lightweight AI-assisted recommendation techniques. The system will operate using curated educational and career-related datasets rather than real-time nationwide institutional integration.
scope_paragraphs.185: The project will not include large-scale production deployment, full national educational coverage, advanced deep-learning-based predictive modelling, or unrestricted conversational AI functionality. These areas are identified as potential future enhancements beyond the scope of Version 1.

methodology: This project adopts Design Science Research (DSR) as the main research methodology because the study involves designing, developing and evaluating a software artefact that addresses a real educational guidance problem. DSR is suitable for Information Systems projects where knowledge is generated through the construction and evaluation of an artefact (Hevner, March, Park, & Ram, 2004).

The project will also use an Agile-inspired iterative prototyping approach for development. DSR provides the research structure, while iterative prototyping supports incremental construction of the knowledge base, recommendation engine, explanation layer, chatbot support and accessibility features.
evaluation_commitment: The prototype will be evaluated using a mixed evaluation approach. Functional testing will check whether the system features work correctly, while scenario-based testing will assess whether recommendations are suitable for different learner profiles. Usability feedback will be collected from adult users where appropriate, using simple rating-scale and open-ended questions.
evaluation_table: Test recommendation relevance using sample learner profiles
Assess clarity, usefulness and ease of use
Assess mobile usability and basic voice-input support
ethics_statement: The project will avoid collecting sensitive personal data and will not involve under-18 participants during evaluation. If feedback is collected, participants will be informed of the purpose of the study, participation will be voluntary, and responses will be anonymised. This aligns with the ethics form requirements relating to informed participation, confidentiality, withdrawal rights and vulnerable groups.
